messages.author: 7dd5d3ef59d0288e
messages.subject: Sampling Frequency
parts:
Hi All,
Thanks for all the support with GGIR on this forum :-)
Can anyone help me with using GGIR on low freqency datasets (12.5Hz).  This would increase the recording time of Axivity watches, but I am not sure if GGIR can handle that?
Thanks in advance for your help,
Cathy

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Sampling Frequency
parts:
GGIR should be able to handle it. If not, let me know.

However, I would not encourage such setting for two reasons:
  • Risk of filtering out true movement components the impact of which may be outcome specific.
  • Possible lack of reliability of Axivity devices at sampling  rates below 50 Hertz. See figure 7 in https://journals.humankinetics.com/view/journals/jmpb/7/1/article-jmpb.2024-0003.xml

Best,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

Thanks as always for your help,
